Knysna.title: Knysna
text: Knysna sits on a large tidal lagoon, with the two sandstone cliffs known as the Heads guarding its narrow mouth to the sea. Indigenous forest runs right up to the edge of town, which gives Knysna a green, tucked-away feel that is different from the open beaches further along the coast.

The waterfront is the social heart of town, with restaurants, craft shops and boat trips. Across the lagoon, Thesen Island and Leisure Isle give you quiet walks and views back to the Heads, and the forest around town has short trails and a boardwalk if you want shade and birdsong.
Knysna is a good base for two or three days. You can combine lagoon time, forest walks and a half-day at the beaches east and west of town without long drives.
highlights: Knysna Heads viewpoint, best at sunset
Featherbed Nature Reserve, reached by ferry
Forest walks and the Garden of Eden boardwalk
Noetzie beach and its stone castles
Oysters and seafood at the waterfront
Knysna.best_time: Spring and autumn are mild and quieter. Summer is the busiest, so book restaurants and boat trips ahead.
Knysna.tip: Go to the Heads viewpoint late afternoon, then have dinner on the waterfront.

things.name: Knysna lagoon cruise
things.note: Boat trips give you birdlife and a close look at the Heads. The lagoon is also home to the endangered Knysna seahorse.

things.name: Featherbed Nature Reserve
things.note: Reached by ferry across the lagoon, with walks and guided tours and views of the Heads.

things.name: Forest walks and the Garden of Eden boardwalk
things.note: Short, shaded walks in indigenous forest. Listen for the Knysna turaco, a colourful forest bird.

things.name: Knysna's forest elephants
things.note: A very small, elusive group survives in the forest. Sightings are extremely rare, so treat it as a story, not a safari.

things.name: Noetzie beach
things.note: A beach below the stone castles, reached on foot. Remember the steep walk back up.

Plett.title: Plettenberg Bay
text: Plettenberg Bay, known as Plett, is the Garden Route's beach town. A long curve of sand looks out over the bay, with mountains behind, and the water is a popular place for swimming, surfing and boat trips.

The Robberg Nature Reserve is the main walking attraction. This rocky peninsula has several hiking routes of different lengths, coastal views and a Cape fur seal colony at the tip. Boat trips from the bay offer dolphin watching, and in winter and spring there is a chance of whales.

Around Plett you will also find wildlife attractions such as Monkeyland and Birds of Eden, river and lagoon outings on the Keurbooms River, and easy access to the forests and coast of Nature's Valley.
highlights: Robberg Nature Reserve hikes and seal colony
Central Beach and the Beacon Island area
Dolphin and whale watching boat trips
Nature's Valley, a short drive east
Plett.best_time: Summer is peak beach season and very busy. Winter and spring are quieter and good for whale watching.
Plett.tip: Hike Robberg in the morning when it is cooler and the light is good, then relax at the beach.

things.name: Robberg Nature Reserve
things.note: A rocky peninsula with several hikes and a Cape fur seal colony at the tip.

things.name: Whale and dolphin boat trips
things.note: Dolphins are seen much of the year, with a chance of whales in winter and spring.

things.name: Monkeyland
things.note: A sanctuary where primates live in forest and are seen on guided walks.

things.name: Birds of Eden
things.note: A very large free-flight aviary under a dome.

things.name: Keurbooms River and lagoon
things.note: Paddling and river trips with birdlife and forested banks.

things.name: Nature's Valley
things.note: Forest and coastline just east of Plett, on the edge of the Tsitsikamma.

George.title: George
text: George is the largest town on the Garden Route and sits at the foot of the Outeniqua Mountains. It is less of a holiday town than its neighbours and more of a working hub, which means good shops, restaurants and services, and a useful base for exploring the region.

The mountains are the draw here. There are forest and mountain trails above town, scenic drives over the Outeniqua and Montagu passes, and local markets on weekends. The coast is close too, with Victoria Bay and Herold's Bay a short drive away for surfing and swimming.
If you want variety, George works well as a central stop: mountains in the morning, beach in the afternoon, and Wilderness or Mossel Bay as easy day trips.
highlights: Victoria Bay and Herold's Bay beaches
George.best_time: Mild year-round. Spring and autumn are good for hiking, and summer for the nearby beaches.
George.tip: Visit the farmers market on Saturday morning, then drive one of the mountain passes.

things.name: Outeniqua mountain trails
things.note: Forest and mountain walks above town.

things.name: Montagu Pass
things.note: A historic mountain pass, popular for scenic drives.

things.name: Garden Route Botanical Garden
things.note: Gardens and easy walks close to town.

things.name: Outeniqua Transport Museum
things.note: Railway history, with old locomotives and carriages.

things.name: Victoria Bay and Herold's Bay
things.note: Small bays on the coast, with surfing at Victoria Bay.

things.name: Birdwatching at the Wilderness lakes
things.note: A short drive east of George, with lakes and river birdlife.

Sedgefield.title: Sedgefield
text: Sedgefield is a small, relaxed town between Wilderness and Knysna, known as a Slow Town. It is popular with people who want a quiet pace, local markets and nature rather than big attractions.

The Swartvlei lagoon is the centre of outdoor life, with kayaking, paddle boarding and birdwatching. A long beach runs along the sea side of town, and the Goukamma Nature Reserve nearby offers walks, dunes and coastal scenery.
Sedgefield is best as a slow stop. Give it a morning or an afternoon around the market, the lagoon and a walk on the beach.
highlights: Wild Oats Community Market on Saturdays
Swartvlei lagoon for kayaking and birds
Sedgefield.best_time: Weekends are the best time for the market. Summer is busiest, and the rest of the year is calm.
Sedgefield.tip: Plan your visit for a Saturday so you can browse the Wild Oats market and then walk on the lagoon or Myoli Beach.

things.name: Swartvlei lagoon
things.note: Kayaking, paddle boarding and good birdwatching.

things.name: Goukamma Nature Reserve
things.note: Dunes, coastline and walking trails just east of town.

things.name: Sedgefield beach walks
things.note: A long beach for easy walks.

things.name: Myoli Beach
things.note: A long, quiet beach on the sea side of town.

Wilderness.title: Wilderness
text: Wilderness is a small coastal village between George and Sedgefield. It has a wide, long beach, a system of lakes and rivers, and forested hills behind, which makes it one of the prettier stops on the Garden Route.

The Map of Africa viewpoint looks over the Kaaimans River as it winds toward the sea, and gets its name from the shape of the river bend. The Wilderness section of the Garden Route National Park has lakes, rivers and bird hides, and you can paddle on the Touw River.
Wilderness is also well known for paragliding and for its beach walks. It works as a half-day stop from George or a quiet base for a night or two.
highlights: Kaaimans River and Touw River kayaking
Lakes and bird hides in the national park
Wilderness.best_time: Spring and early summer are lovely for walking and kayaking. Summer is busiest on the beach.
Wilderness.tip: Do the Map of Africa viewpoint early in the day, then walk along the beach.

things.name: Map of Africa viewpoint
things.note: A short walk to a lookout over the bend of the Kaaimans River.

things.name: Touw River kayaking
things.note: Paddle through the river and forest, with birdlife on the banks.

things.name: Bird hides in the national park
things.note: Lakes and rivers with hides for birdwatching.

things.name: Paragliding
things.note: Flights from the hills above the village.

things.name: Wilderness beach walks
things.note: A very long beach for walking.

Mossel Bay.title: Mossel Bay
text: Mossel Bay is a historic harbour town at the western end of the Garden Route. It has one of the longest stories of any town on the coast, linked to early Portuguese sailors and the Dias Museum Complex.

The Cape St Blaize lighthouse sits on the cliffs above town, with a walking path beneath it that gives coastal views and a look at old caves. Beaches such as Santos are good for swimming, and boat trips go out to see the seals at Seal Island.
Mossel Bay works well as a first or last stop on a Garden Route trip, with history, beaches and sea activities close together.
highlights: Cape St Blaize lighthouse and cliff walk
Mossel Bay.best_time: Summer for the beaches and boat trips. Autumn and spring are quieter and still pleasant.
Mossel Bay.tip: Walk the cliff path below the lighthouse in the late afternoon for the best light.

things.name: Seal Island boat trips
things.note: Boat trips out to see the Cape fur seals.

things.name: Cape St Blaize cliff walk
things.note: A cliff path below the lighthouse with coastal views and old caves.

things.name: Dias Museum Complex
things.note: Maritime history in the old part of town.

things.name: Pinnacle Point
things.note: An archaeological area nearby, linked to early human history.

things.name: Santos Beach
things.note: A swimming beach close to the town centre.

Hartenbos.title: Hartenbos
text: Hartenbos is a relaxed seaside resort right next to Mossel Bay, popular with families for its long, gently sloping beach and calm lagoon.
It suits a slow holiday. Children can paddle in the lagoon, there are easy walks along the shore, and the river mouth is a good place to look for birds.
Hartenbos is close enough to Mossel Bay to combine with its museums, seal boat trips and cliff walks, which makes it a quieter base for a few days.
highlights: Mossel Bay attractions a short drive away
Hartenbos.best_time: Summer is the busiest family season. Autumn and spring are calmer and still pleasant.
Hartenbos.tip: Visit the lagoon in the morning when it is quiet and the birds are active.

things.name: Hartenbos beach
things.note: A long, gently sloping beach that suits families.

things.name: Hartenbos lagoon
things.note: Calm water for paddling, with birds around the river mouth.

things.name: Shoreline walks
things.note: Easy walks along the coast with sea views.

Great Brak River.title: Great Brak River
text: Great Brak River is a small riverside village between Mossel Bay and George, built around a lagoon where the river meets the sea. Little Brak River, its neighbour, sits a few kilometres west on its own estuary.

The lagoons are calm and sheltered, which makes them good for paddling, picnics and birdwatching, and the beaches are quieter than in the bigger resorts. The village also has a small museum about its local history.
It makes a gentle stop along the coast: a walk by the river, a swim, and lunch before you carry on to George or Mossel Bay.
highlights: Great Brak River lagoon and beach
Great Brak River.best_time: Summer is best for swimming. The rest of the year is quiet and good for walks.
Great Brak River.tip: Stop for a lagoon walk and lunch, then carry on to George or Mossel Bay.

things.name: Great Brak River lagoon
things.note: Sheltered water for paddling and birdwatching.

things.name: Little Brak River estuary
things.note: A quiet estuary just west of the village.

things.name: Great Brak River Museum
things.note: A small museum about the village and its history.

Nature's Valley.title: Nature's Valley
text: Nature's Valley is a tiny, secluded village at the foot of the Groot River Pass, set between the Salt River, the forested Tsitsikamma foothills, the sea and the Groot River lagoon. It lies in the de Vasselot section of the Tsitsikamma National Park, roughly 30 km from Plett.
There is almost no commercial development, so the attractions are the golden beach, the lagoon and the forest walks. It is also where the five-day Otter Trail finishes.
The road down the pass is steep and winding, which is one reason the village stays so quiet. Services are very limited, so bring food and supplies with you.
highlights: Forest walks in the de Vasselot section
The end of the Otter Trail
Nature's Valley.best_time: Spring and autumn are mild and quiet. Summer is busier with holiday homes.
Nature's Valley.tip: Bring snacks and supplies, as services are very limited.

things.name: Nature's Valley beach and lagoon
things.note: A golden beach with the Groot River lagoon beside it.

things.name: de Vasselot forest walks
things.note: Forest trails inside the Tsitsikamma National Park.

things.name: Otter Trail finish
things.note: The five-day hiking trail ends here after starting at Storms River Mouth.

things.name: Groot River Pass
things.note: A winding pass built in the 1800s, with big forest trees along the road.

Storms River.title: Storms River
text: Storms River village is the gateway to the Tsitsikamma National Park and the main Garden Route village in the Eastern Cape. It sits among tall trees and mountains just off the N2, and it is the adventure stop of the route.

The park is about 5 km from the village and is known for its forested coastline and marine reserve. Storms River Mouth, where the suspension bridges are, is also where the Otter Trail starts. Back in the village you can try canopy tours and other adventure activities.
Give the park most of a day, and book popular activities ahead in peak season, because the village is small.
Storms River.best_time: Spring and autumn are comfortable for walking. Summer is busy, so book activities ahead.
Storms River.tip: Go to Storms River Mouth early and give it most of a day.

things.name: Storms River Mouth suspension bridges
things.note: Walkways over the river mouth in the Tsitsikamma National Park.

things.name: Otter Trail
things.note: A five-day coastal hiking trail that starts at Storms River Mouth.

things.name: Canopy tours
things.note: Slides through the forest canopy near the village.

things.name: Bloukrans Bridge bungee
things.note: A famous bungee jump, a short drive west of the village.

things.name: Cycling to Storms River Mouth
things.note: A cycle route from the village through the old pass to a viewpoint over the mouth.

Oudtshoorn.title: Oudtshoorn
text: Oudtshoorn lies inland in the Klein Karoo, over the Outeniqua Mountains from George. It is best known for its ostrich farms and the Cango Caves, and it adds a very different, drier landscape to a Garden Route trip.
The drive over the mountains is part of the attraction. The Swartberg Pass and Meiringspoort are well-known scenic routes, and wildlife visits include the ostrich farms and the Cango Wildlife Ranch.
Many people visit on a day trip from George or Mossel Bay, but staying a night lets you take the passes slowly.
Oudtshoorn.best_time: Spring and autumn are the most comfortable. Summers inland can be very hot.
Oudtshoorn.tip: Start early to avoid the heat and give the passes plenty of time.

things.name: Cango Caves
things.note: Large limestone caves with guided tours.

things.name: Ostrich farms
things.note: Tours of working farms, the area's best-known attraction.

things.note: A wildlife park near town.
